story:
Tezcatlipoca was one of four sons born to Ometecuhtli and Omecihuatl, the primordial lord and lady of duality. Together with his brothers Quetzalcoatl, Huitzilopochtli, and Xipe Totec, called the Black, White, Blue, and Red Tezcatlipocas, he helped create all the other gods, the world, and humanity. His animal counterpart was the jaguar, and in that form he became known as Tepeyollotl.

In the myth of the Five Suns, Tezcatlipoca ruled the first creation, the Sun of Earth, but Quetzalcoatl struck him down, destroying that world and transforming Tezcatlipoca into a jaguar. Quetzalcoatl then ruled the next creation, the Sun of Water, until Tezcatlipoca struck him down in turn, destroying the third creation, the Sun of Wind. The two gods were rivals but also collaborators, both instrumental in the various creations of the world.

In the legends of the city of Tollan, Tezcatlipoca deceived Quetzalcoatl, who ruled that city, and forced him into exile.

In another creation account, Quetzalcoatl and Tezcatlipoca joined forces to make the world. Before their act, there was only the sea and a primordial crocodilian earth monster called Cipactli. To lure her, Tezcatlipoca offered his own foot as bait, and Cipactli ate it, losing him his foot. The two gods then captured her and distorted her body to form the land.

The central figure was one of four offspring born to a primordial lord and lady of duality. Together with three sibling deities, given color designations of black, white, blue, and red, he helped create all the other gods, the world, and humanity. His animal counterpart was a great spotted wildcat, and in that form he became known by another name, meaning "mountain heart."

In a myth of successive world-ages, the central figure ruled the first creation, the age of Earth, but a rival culture-hero deity struck him down, destroying that world and transforming him into the wildcat. The rival deity then ruled the next creation, the age of Water, until the central figure struck him down in turn, destroying the third creation, the age of Wind. The two gods were rivals but also collaborators, both instrumental in the various creations of the world.

In legends of a certain city, the central figure deceived the rival deity, who ruled that city, and forced him into exile.

In another creation account, the rival deity and the central figure joined forces to make the world. Before their act, there was only the sea and a primordial crocodilian earth monster. To lure her, the central figure offered his own foot as bait, and the monster ate it, losing him his foot. The two gods then captured her and distorted her body to form the land.
